source_findings.finding: main runs startup files before evaluating the -c command body. Its outer gate excludes real/effective UID or GID mismatch via running_setuid; this is different from privileged_mode.

The early remote-startup path checks noninteractive, no_rc unset, nonlogin, not named sh, a -c command and shell_level below2. It does not check privileged_mode. SSH variables or isnetconn can select execute_bashrc_file.
The later BASH_ENV path explicitly requires privileged_mode zero. The --norc option sets no_rc, preventing the earlier remote-startup path; -p alone does not impose that check.
In the getpeername branch, failed calls return false only for ENOTSOCK, ENOTCONN, EINVAL or EBADF. Other errors, including EPERM, classify the descriptor as network-connected.
